header:
Date: 2026-09-07T15:00:00Z
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Lewis Park (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (CTO - Celestia Energy), Diego Martinez (Lead ML Eng), Sophie Lin (Prod Mgr)
Recording id: rwd-20260907-5829
Location: Zoom
Notes: Discovery focused on model selection (open models), context length requirements, multilingual support, and tool-calling (retrieval + db writes).
summary: Celestia Energy is evaluating Redwood for an RAG-heavy product that needs long contexts (target 50k–150k tokens native, with sharding/streaming fallback), multilingual responses (English, Spanish, Japanese), and secure tool-calling (retrieval, external API calls, and transactional DB updates). Primary evaluation axes: latency SLOs, unit cost per token, data residency/KMS, and ease of private deployment. Action: price comparison, security docs, technical deep dive and benchmarks.
topics: Current infra and authentication (GCP, VPC, SSO)
Context length and sharding strategies (50k–150k target)
Open model comparisons (Mistral, Llama-3 variants, Falcon)
Tool-calling: retrieval, external APIs, DB writes, and safety controls
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem/VPC)
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maria, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Lewis Park our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Anika Rao (CTO - Celestia): Hi, Anika here.
[00:11] Diego Martinez (Lead ML Eng): Diego.
[00:12] Sophie Lin (Product): Sophie.
[00:15] Maria: Great, thanks. Agenda — quick context from you, then we'll walk through model options, context lengths, tool-calling, and deployment modes. Sound good?
[00:24] Anika: Yep. We're moving fast, want to decide by end of month. Key constraints: data residency for EU customers, SOC 2 is a must, and very sensitive telemetry we can't leave in a third-party blob.
[00:35] Diego: From engineering side, we currently run a retrieval stack with Pinecone for vectors, and prefiltering. We want the LLM to do multi-turn RAG across large documents — like full equipment manuals, regulatory sets. So long contexts matter.
[00:49] Sophie: Product wants Spanish and Japanese support, and the ability for the model to call our internal tools to fetch live telemetry and also write status updates back to our change log — so tool-calling with transactional safety.
[01:05] Lewis (SE): Quick clarifying question — when you say 'long' contexts, can you give a ballpark token size or number of documents?
[01:12] Diego: We're targeting 50k tokens in the short term, aiming for 150k in the next 6–9 months if feasible. Not sure if that means sharding or a single 150k context model.
[01:24] Maria: OK, great. We'll cover two ways: model-native long context (64k/100k variants) and shard+retrieval approaches with KV caching. Note: our runtime handles KV cache and prefix caching — sometimes transcript shows K V cache as K V cash in auto text — sorry.
[01:38] Anika: Haha, no worries. Another compliance note — we have an on-prem HSM and need KMS integration for keys.
[01:44] Lewis: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping — we can share specifics in the security doc.
[01:52] [01:52] Maria: All right, let's go into model choices. Diego, Sophie — what are your priorities: raw generation quality, latency, or cost?
[01:59] Diego: Quality for RAG and hallucination avoidance is top, then latency. Cost matters but we can trade off with dedicated capacity.
[02:07] Sophie: For product, predictable latency — UI needs under 1.2s p50 for short queries and less than 4s for large context operations.
[02:16] Lewis: Notes: p50 targets are helpful. For open models, there are tradeoffs. Llama-3 variants tend to be strong on instruction following and are available in higher context lengths in community forks; Mistral-70B has good throughput but may need quantization profiles; Falcon is cost-effective at scale. We usually recommend starting small with a hosted open-model baseline, then move to dedicated if throughput/latency or data residency requires.
[02:42] [02:42] Anika: Can Redwood host EU-only endpoints? We need data to stay in Frankfurt region.
[02:48] Maria: Yes, Hosted can be region-restricted and our enterprise partnerships include EU-only tenancy. For strict residency and private control you can choose Dedicated with VPC peering or Private (VPC or on-prem).
[02:59] Diego: About tool-calling — we have microservices exposed internally; we need authenticated calls from the model runtime, plus a retry/backoff pattern and idempotency for DB writes.
[03:12] Lewis: We support function-calling patterns with signed short-lived credentials and can broker calls via a private connector in Private/Dedicated modes. For hosted, we use customer-signed webhooks but we understand that's less ideal for writes to sensitive systems.
[03:26] Sophie: Are there guardrails to prevent accidental destructive writes?
[03:29] Lewis: Yes — you can require a two-step flow: model suggests an action, the action gets reviewed by a middleware or a human approval step. We also have RBAC and route-level tracing for audit logs.
[03:41] [03:41] Anika: Good. SOC 2 and audit logs are, again, must-haves. Also, how do we reason about KV cache with sharded context vs native long context?
[03:51] Lewis: With sharding we keep a retrieval layer that fetches relevant chunks and then we stitch via streaming. KV cache is per-session to speed up prefix tokens. Native long-context models remove some complexity but are more expensive per token and need specialized kernels. It also depends on your latency SLOs.
[04:10] Diego: What's the typical cost difference? Rough numbers are fine.
[04:13] Maria: High level: hosted with 64k native models will be higher per token than a dedciated quantized instance; dedicated reserved pricing amortizes GPU costs and can be 30–60% cheaper at scale depending on utilization. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[04:30] Sophie: You said 'dedciated' — did you mean dedicated? The transcript spelled it that way earlier, haha.
[04:34] Maria: Yep, my bad, Redwood Dedicated. 
[04:37] [04:37] Anika: For multilingual — do we need separate models per language or does one multi-lingual model perform well?
[04:44] Lewis: Many open models are multilingual out of the box, but performance varies: Llama-3 family often does well in English and Spanish, Japanese can be hit-or-miss. Mistral fine-tuned multilingual variants or having a language-specific reranker can help. Retrieval helps a lot for domain-specific content irrespective of language.
[05:02] Diego: For evaluation, we have prompt sets in English and Spanish now, Japanese coming. We'll share examplars.
[05:08] Maria: Great — please send. We'll use those for benchmarks.
[05:11] [05:11] Sophie: On retrieval vector store — we use Pinecone now, could we keep it and have Redwood call it, or should we migrate?
[05:17] Lewis: You can keep Pinecone. Redwood can call external vector stores or host an internal retrieval service. For Private deployments it's common to keep vector store internal for data residency. For Hosted, we offer connectors.
[05:28] Anika: Timeline — we want an initial pilot in 4 weeks, production in Q1. Is that realistic?
[05:33] Maria: Yes, a 4-week pilot is reasonable for a focused use case (subset of docs, defined evals). Production by Q1 depends on the pilot outcome and legal sign-off.
[05:44] [05:44] Diego: For the pilot, can we run a small benchmark that measures p50, p95 and token cost across 30k/64k contexts?
[05:52] Lewis: Absolutely. We'll propose a benchplan: 30k prompt/64k prompt with both shard+retrieval and native long-context models. We'll test Mistral-70B, Llama-3-70B (if available with 64k variant), and a quantized Falcon variant.
[06:08] Maria: I'm going to list risks we heard: (1) Data residency/KMS, (2) Latency SLOs with native long contexts, (3) Tool-calling safety for writes, (4) Cost at scale. Does that align?
[06:19] Anika: Yes, and add auditing and exportability of logs.
[06:23] [06:23] Sophie: Quick question about model rollouts — can we do canary and automatic fallback to cheaper models if load spikes?
[06:29] Lewis: Yes, our rollout tool supports canary percentages, A/B by route, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or a cheaper tier if latency/backlog is detected.
[06:39] Diego: When you fallback, how do you ensure output consistency? We need guard rails as product depends on deterministic behavior for some ops.
[06:47] Lewis: You can pin model versions per route. Fallbacks are to compatible model families; we also log diffs and can surface quality regressions. For high-consistency routes, you can disable automatic fallback.
[07:01] [07:01] Maria: Let's touch on security docs — you'll need SOC 2 report, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and our private deployment checklist. We'll send a package.
[07:11] Anika: Also need SSO/SAML and RBAC integration with our identity provider.
[07:16] Lewis: We have SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and route-level RBAC. Private deployments can use your directory via VPC peering and private connectors.
[07:25] [07:25] Sophie: About billing and observability — product wants token-level cost breakdowns per route and per team.
[07:32] Maria: We provide per-token cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks so you can map requests to teams. That's part of Redwood Console.
[07:41] Diego: One more technical: streaming vs batch when you have large context — is streaming used with sharding?
[07:47] Lewis: Yes, streaming works with sharded retrieval; the runtime can stream partial results while remaining tokens are fetched. It's a tradeoff: streaming reduces perceived latency but can complicate context merging.
[07:59] [07:59] Anika: If we need private on-prem deployments, what's the timeline and footprint?
[08:04] Lewis: On-prem requires validated hardware and network setup; typical engagement is 8–12 weeks with our deployment engineers, shorter for VPC models. We'll share the on-prem checklist.
[08:14] Maria: Okay, let's go into a short demo of cost tradeoffs — high-level numbers only.
[08:19] [08:19] Maria shares screen (deck): quick pricing sketch.
[08:24] Diego: Can you show the math for 100 qps at 64k?
[08:28] Maria: Rough calc: native 64k models—higher memory and specialized kernels—cost per token can be 2–3x standard 8k models. For sustained 100 qps, Dedicated reserved capacity tends to amortize to much lower cost. We'll include the spreadsheet.
[08:42] [08:42] Sophie: Any case studies of customers with 100k+ context or multilingual RAG?
[08:47] Lewis: We have a couple anonymized references in energy and fintech who use 64k native and sharded pipelines; I can share the one-pagers.
[08:55] [08:55] Anika: Okay — any blockers from legal or procurement you anticipate?
[08:58] Maria: Standard enterprise contract, export control checks for certain models — we'll flag any model-specific export issues. Also procurement may request SLAs for Dedicated.
[09:09] Diego: On the model side, do you support quantized execution (INT8/4-bit) for our heavier workloads?
[09:15] Lewis: Yes, our runtime supports quantization-friendly paths and we have profiling to recommend quantization profiles. For some models quantization affects quality, we measure that as part of the bench.
[09:26] Sophie: For tool-calling, can we get an end-to-end example that shows the model calling a retrieval endpoint and then making an authenticated DB write?
[09:33] Lewis: We'll design a sample flow: model -> retrieval -> function-call (signed token) -> middleware with idempotency -> DB update. For hosted we'll use signed webhooks; for Private/Dedicated we'll use short-lived credentials via your KMS.
[09:48] [09:48] Anika: Sounds good. What's the next step on scheduling the technical deep dive?
[09:53] Maria: We'll propose next week Tuesday or Thursday for a 60-min SE session. Lewis, are you good for the bench ops?
[09:59] Lewis: Yep, I'll lead the bench and need Diego's prompt sets and sample dataset.
[10:04] Diego: I'll upload to the shared drive and send link today.
[10:08] [10:08] Maria: Recap — Maria to send price sheet and security package; Lewis to propose bench plan and run initial tests; Diego to share prompts/dataset; schedule technical deep dive. Any other open questions?
[10:20] Sophie: Minor — do you keep the model logs for how long in hosted? Retention policy?
[10:26] Maria: By default hosted logs retained 30 days; enterprise plans can extend retention or disable logs for private-only. We'll include that in the security doc.
[10:36] [10:36] Anika: Also, can we get an estimate for ramping Dedicated capacity — like min GPU footprint?
[10:41] Lewis: Minimum depends on model family; for 70B models expect a few A100-equivalents for redundancy; we'll provide sizing guidance.
[10:50] Maria: OK, thanks everyone. We'll follow up within 48 hours with the items discussed.
[10:55] [10:55] — end of call —

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions sometimes labeled 'Speaker 2' in middle sections; some technical terms were slightly transcribed (e.g., 'K V cache' as 'K V cash').
